summary: SL-068 was meant to record sort-on-read in two places: the engine's Scan Store architecture line and a repo doc. Sort-on-read was already built and green (9-44 ms Core read against a 250 ms budget). The loop wrote docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md, a pointer line in the SL-042 doc, and an 8-case check script, and fixed three minor sourcing errors in the doc. The headline deliverable, the engine record edit, was not done: no stage has a write path to it, so it passed with criterion 1 UNMET per a person's answer (Q-123). The engine's line still says 'stored sorted largest first', which is the staleness the slice existed to remove.

payload.summary: SL-068 was meant to record sort-on-read in two places: the engine's Scan Store architecture line and a repo doc. Sort-on-read was already built and green (9-44 ms Core read against a 250 ms budget). The loop wrote docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md, a pointer line in the SL-042 doc, and an 8-case check script, and fixed three minor sourcing errors in the doc. The headline deliverable, the engine record edit, was not done: no stage has a write path to it, so it passed with criterion 1 UNMET per a person's answer (Q-123). The engine's line still says 'stored sorted largest first', which is the staleness the slice existed to remove.
payload.estimate_error: The size and tier were wrong in kind. The doc work was small (one doc, two pointer lines), so 'medium, low risk' fit it. The slice's main deliverable was an edit outside the worktree, and SL-042 had already shown no stage can make one. The slice was therefore mostly a hand-off, not a build. The 'low' tier also skipped critique and critique-review. The doc's risk was wrong sources for figures and citations, and one of the three sourcing errors got past code-review round 1. The cost was build x2, code-review x3, validate x4, and criterion 1 still unmet.
what_went_wrong: The slice was cut to do something the loop cannot do. SL-042's build hit the same missing write path, build-check #1 halted on it, and the design raised it as its one open question. A person answered it (Q-123) only at validate #4. Criterion 1 ended UNMET, so the next slice's prompt still reads 'stored sorted largest first'.

The design's open question on acceptance was whether validate may pass with the engine-record edit unapplied. It was raised at design #1, and design #2 passed without an answer. The build, code review and validate #3 then carried it, and validate #3 halted on it. It should have been answered before build.

Two of the three review findings copied provenance errors. The '9-40 ms' figure in the brief is not a range. SL-042's reflect-1.json:74 joined validate's 9.16-9.80 ms with the build's 35.9-40.2 ms. The build wrote 'the brief rounded this to 9-40', which is wrong (m1). The design's own text credited '~136 MiB headroom SL-042's spike measured', but the only source is reflect-1.json:84, which says it was a throwaway layout and that SL-042 then spent 96 MiB (R2-m3). Neither figure was traced to its ledger file before it was quoted.

Code-review round 1 filed m1 and m2 but missed R2-m3. The mis-sourced 136 MiB survived until round 2, and round 2 was the pass that checked each citation against its source. That is the check round 1 should have done.

Routing cost two validate runs. Code review passed with three fixes accepted-pending, so nothing had been applied. Validate #1 halted, and validate #2 then found 'the fixes were never made' and bounced to build. The pending fixes could have gone straight to build.

The design said docs-only, 'add no new test', and expected the diff to touch only docs/design. The build satisfied its eight material [case] obligations with a standalone tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1 that regex-checks the doc's prose. It was then edited again in attempt 2 (C-004 went from 17 to 19 checks). C-008 was rewritten to allow the script, and code review reported 'nothing new departed from the design'.

The rule-before-result claim could not be shown from git. The SL-042 doc's rule (line 45), its figures (line 88) and its design record all first appear in b5c2b62. Only the .taad ledger timestamps show ordering (design #29 at 17:23:45Z, build #1 at 23:47:34Z). The design imported this as 'must-verify' and assumed git would show it.

learned.lesson: No stage can edit the engine's architecture record, so do not cut a slice whose deliverable is that edit. It is a human task. Slice criteria that live outside the worktree should be marked 'hand-off' at open, not sized as build work.
learned.evidence: SL-042 build could not edit it. SL-068 build-check #1 halted on it. Build attempt 2 reported 'still not applied', and validate #3 said 'no stage can read or write it'. Validate #4 passed only by recording criterion 1 as UNMET under Q-123.

learned.lesson: To show 'X was decided before Y' inside an SL-0xx slice, use the .taad/slices ledger timestamps, not git. SL-042's design, build and doc all land in one commit.
learned.evidence: O-001 and O-007: rule at line 45, figures at line 88 and design-slice-29.json all first appear in b5c2b62. The ledger dates design #29 at 2026-09-25T17:23:45Z and build #1 at 23:47:34Z.

learned.lesson: Do not treat '9-40 ms' as a range or as a baseline for a tighter trigger. Release reads of the 100,000-child ChildrenLargestFirst are bimodal on this PC, about 9-11 ms in some runs and 33-44 ms in others. Only the 250 ms budget (at least 5.7x margin) has held across every run. Debug is slower again, about 21-24 ms in one run.
learned.evidence: Build-check runs 8.98-44.12 ms, with reads dropping from about 35 to 9-10 ms in the last two positions of each run. Validate runs 9.08-14.54 ms and 8.77-10.84 ms. The Debug default suite gave 20.62-24.07 ms. The brief's '9-40' is a join of two SL-042 stages (reflect-1.json:74).

learned.lesson: Figures in slice briefs and reflection summaries lose their provenance when a reflection joins runs from different stages. Before a doc quotes one, trace it to the ledger file and line, for example .taad/slices/SL-042/reflect-1.json:74 and :84 and validate-slice-1.json. Do not describe its origin from memory.
learned.evidence: m1: the brief's 9-40 was described as a rounding of this slice's runs. R2-m3: '136 MiB' was credited to a spike that did not measure it. Both were fixed only after review, against reflect-1.json:74 and :84.

learned.lesson: FolderTreeNode keeps an ordered Children array for every folder opened, until the next scan. 'Sort-on-read, nothing stored' is true of ScanStore only. Any stored-order or live-refresh work has to invalidate those window-held arrays as well as the store's temporary index.
learned.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/FolderTreeNode.cs:14-16 ('kept until the next scan') and :142-158 (`Children = nodes`, early return on later opens). Finding m2. The doc's Not covered section now names them.

learned.lesson: The engine's Scan Store line has other stale content besides the child-order clause: 699 MiB peak and 572 MB store against SL-044's as-built 652 MiB. SL-068 deliberately did not audit it, so it will still mislead a memory-related slice.
learned.evidence: Design decision 7 and case C-011. The doc says the memory figures are not re-audited. SL-042 spent 96 MiB retained of the earlier layout's ~136 MiB headroom.

learned.lesson: For docs slices made of figures and citations, code review should check each cited figure against its file:line source in round 1. Round 2 did exactly that and found nothing new, while round 1 had missed R2-m3. A 'low' tier skips critique, so code review is the only sourcing check.
learned.evidence: Critique and critique-review were skipped by the low-risk sizing. Code-review round 1 filed m1 and m2. R2-m3 appeared only in round 2, which checked every new citation against reflect-1.json:74 and :84 and FolderTreeNode.cs.

learned.lesson: When code review disposes findings as accepted-pending, send the slice straight to build. Routing it through validate first cost two validate runs to learn the fixes were not made.
learned.evidence: Code-review #2 passed with three accepted-pending findings. Validate #1 halted, and validate #2 failed with 'the fixes were never made' and sent the slice to build-slice #2.

missed.what: Round 1 did not check where the doc's '~136 MiB headroom SL-042's spike measured' came from. SL-042's reflect-1.json:84 calls it a throwaway layout's headroom, of which SL-042 spent 96 MiB. The doc therefore presented as available headroom that is mostly spent, and credited it to the wrong source. The design's rationale carried the same wording, and critique did not run.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 2 (R2-m3), owed to build attempt 2

missed.what: The design's docs-only case expected the diff to touch only docs/design paths, and its decisions said 'add no new test'. The build added tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1, a standalone script with eight cases of roughly 10-19 prose checks each, and later edited it. C-008 was changed to allow the script. All three code-review rounds reported 'nothing new departed from the design'.
missed.caught_by: nothing; surfaced only in this reflection by comparing the design's case with the diff

missed.what: The design's open question was whether validate may pass with the engine-record edit unapplied. It went unanswered through design, build and code review. Critique, which was skipped by sizing, was the gate that could have forced an answer before build, and it did not run. The question only got an answer at validate #4 (Q-123), after validate ran four times.
missed.caught_by: validate-slice #3, which halted on it; a person answered it at validate #4

unknowns: What the engine's Scan Store architecture line reads today. No stage has read it; 'still says stored sorted largest first' is inferred from SL-042's reflect-1.json:74.
Whether the engine will ever give a stage a write path to its architecture record, or whether such edits are permanently manual. This decides whether a slice like SL-068 can be cut again.

Why the 100,000-child Release read is bimodal (about 9-11 ms in some runs, 33-44 ms in others), whether from machine load, tiered JIT or GC. It needs settling before any budget tighter than 250 ms is set.

Whether live refresh needs a stored order or only cheaper invalidation of the window's kept Children arrays. SL-044 measured the refresh median at 84 ms against a 50 ms bar, and this slice put it out of scope.

The reopen condition 'cold open of 100,000 children reaches 500 ms' has no unattended check. Only the 250 ms Core test runs by default, and the on-screen figures (97.9-141.9 ms) come from a manual --report.

candidates.title: Apply the submitted find/replace to the engine's Scan Store architecture line and report the text found
candidates.why: Criterion 1 ended UNMET. The exact edit is at docs/design/SL-068-sort-on-read.md:116-125, and the engine's line still says children are 'stored sorted largest first'. The next slice's prompt is built from that line. It is a person's task, since no stage can write the record. Afterwards, change the doc's Status line from 'not applied'.

candidates.title: Decide how engine-record edits get made: a stage write path, or a standing manual step outside slices
candidates.why: SL-042 (m9) and SL-068 both got stuck on the same missing write path. Without a decision, the next reflection that wants a record corrected will raise another unbuildable candidate.

candidates.title: Re-audit the memory figures in the engine's Scan Store line (699 MiB peak, 572 MB store) against the as-built 652 MiB
candidates.why: SL-068 replaced only the child-order clause and left these figures stale, and the doc says so. The 136 MiB headroom framing is also mostly spent (96 MiB retained by SL-042). Any memory-related slice will read the stale line.

candidates.title: Keep, wire into a suite, or delete tests/bugs/SL-068-DecisionCases.ps1
candidates.why: It is a standalone script with regex checks on the wording of one design doc, and nothing runs it unattended. Its checks (for example C-004's origin sentence) may fail once someone edits the doc, such as flipping the 'not applied' status when the engine edit lands. The design said 'no new test'.

candidates.title: Scope live-refresh work to include invalidating FolderTreeNode's kept Children arrays and the 84 ms re-sort against the 50 ms bar
candidates.why: Finding m2 showed the window keeps an ordered array per opened folder until the next scan (FolderTreeNode.cs:14-16, 142-158). SL-068's Not covered section defers the refresh question, and any refresh design has to handle both the store's temporary index and these arrays.
